verifiedClaims.claim: The Most Dangerous Roads and Intersections in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina
verifiedClaims.currentValue: By crash COUNT the superlatives partly hold: SCDPS ranks US-17 Horry County's No. 1 roadway every year 2020-2024 (1,821 collisions, 9 fatal in 2024) and US-501 No. 2 (1,462); Horry was 4th of 46 counties in total collisions and 3rd in fatal collisions in 2024. By RATE they do not: Horry's 2024 mileage death rate was 1.516 per 100 million VMT, below the statewide 1.68 (2023: 1.704 vs 1.72). Of the post's seven numbered intersections, only two appear in any Horry County Top-5 table 2020-2024 (SC-9 at Hwy 57; US-501 at Carolina Forest Blvd), one is Georgetown County's No. 1 (US-17 at SC-707, Murrells Inlet), and four (US-501/SC-31, the Back Gate, Oak Forest/Pine Island, US-17 Bypass/Wood Thrush) never appear.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS South Carolina Traffic Collision Fact Book, 2024 Edition (Horry County, Part VI pp. 137-138; PDF pp. 145-146)
verifiedClaims.note: NOT a patcher-editable surface (title is not in body.html) — for the owner. 'Most Dangerous' is defensible only as 'highest-crash by count', and only if the numbered list is re-ordered to the SCDPS tables (SC-9 at Hwy 57 first) and the four untraceable intersections are dropped or re-framed. Suggested title: "Myrtle Beach's Highest-Crash Roads and Intersections: What the State Data Shows". If the title stays, the body must define 'dangerous' as SCDPS collision counts and FARS fatal-crash counts.

verifiedClaims.claim: The Myrtle Beach area and the Grand Strand attract more than 20 million visitors annually, and that massive influx of tourist traffic transforms the region's roads into some of the most dangerous in South Carolina.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Myrtle Beach Area CVB 'Fast Facts': 18.2 million annual visitors (2024 estimate per D.K. Shifflet). The Chamber reported 2025 tourism down 3% and projected a further ~3% dip in 2026 (WPDE, 2026-03-09). Horry County: 4th of 46 SC counties in total collisions (11,103) and 3rd in fatal collisions (58) in 2024, but its mileage death rate (1.516) was below the state's 1.68.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Myrtle Beach Area CVB — Industry Research (Fast Facts); WPDE 2026-03-09; SCDPS Fact Book 2024
verifiedClaims.note: 'More than 20 million' is not supported by the destination's own figure. Suggested: 'The Grand Strand draws about 18 million visitors a year (18.2 million in 2024, per the Myrtle Beach Area CVB), and Horry County ranks among South Carolina's highest-crash counties — 4th of 46 for total collisions and 3rd for fatal collisions in 2024.' Avoid 'some of the most dangerous' unless framed by count. WPDE: https://wpde.com/news/local/grand-strand-tourism-down-three-percent-surfside-myrtlebeach

verifiedClaims.claim: Horry County, which encompasses Myrtle Beach, Conway, and Murrells Inlet, consistently ranks among the top counties in the state for total traffic collisions, injuries, and fatalities.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Ranking verified: Horry was 4th in total collisions every year 2019-2024; fatal-collision rank 1st (2019), 4th (2020), 3rd (2021), 2nd (2022), 4th (2023), 3rd (2024); serious-injury collisions 3rd in 2020-2024. But Murrells Inlet is not in Horry County: the U.S. Census geocoder places the Murrells Inlet CDP (and the firm's 631 Bellamy Ave office) in Georgetown County.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Books, 2020-2024 editions (Horry County Top 5 Roadways/Intersections page in each); U.S. Census Bureau Geocoder
verifiedClaims.note: Replace 'Murrells Inlet' with an Horry community: '...which encompasses Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Conway and Surfside Beach...'. Rankings clause keeps. Census geocoder: https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/geographies/address?street=631+Bellamy+Ave&city=Murrells+Inlet&state=SC&zip=29576&benchmark=Public_AR_Current&vintage=Current_Current&format=json (the same county discrepancy in client.json was escalated in facts-4738).

verifiedClaims.currentValue: US-17 alone carried 1,821 of Horry County's 11,103 collisions in 2024 (16.4%) and US-501 another 1,462 (13.2%).

verifiedClaims.claim: The Grand Strand's population effectively triples during peak summer months.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No CVB, Chamber, Census or SCDOT source gives a seasonal population multiplier for the Grand Strand. The CVB publishes annual visitors (18.2 million, 2024) only.

verifiedClaims.claim: Many of the Myrtle Beach area's busiest roads — particularly U.S. 17 (Kings Highway) and U.S. 501 — were not designed to handle their current traffic volumes.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDOT 2025 AADT: US 17 between SC 707 (Socastee Blvd) and US 501 — 82,200 vehicles/day; US 501 between SC 31 and the US 17 Bypass — 65,900; US 501 SC 544-SC 31 — 54,900. Horry County's RIDE III program funds 'U.S. Hwy. 501 Corridor improvements — SC Hwy. 31 to SC 544' (six-lane widening and signalized-intersection improvements), and a US 501 widening from Gardner Lacy Rd to SC 544 is in the GSATS program.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDOT Average Daily Traffic, Horry County, 2025; GSATS Policy Committee packet 2025-08-01
verifiedClaims.note: 'Not designed to handle' is an engineering conclusion no source states. Suggested: 'Many of the busiest roads carry very heavy volumes — about 82,000 vehicles a day on U.S. 17 near Socastee Boulevard and 66,000 on U.S. 501 east of S.C. 31 (SCDOT, 2025) — and U.S. 501 is in line for widening under the county's RIDE III program.' GSATS: https://cms3.revize.com/revize/waccamawgsats/Documents/Boards%20And%20Commissions/South%20Carolina/Policy%20Committee/Packets/Policy%20Meeting%20Packet%208.01.2025.pdf

verifiedClaims.claim: Pedestrian fatalities along the Grand Strand are a persistent and tragic problem.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: SCDPS 2024: Horry County crashes injured or killed 110 pedestrians, 12 fatally. FARS 2020-2024: 94 of Horry County's 328 fatal crashes (28.7%) involved a person outside a vehicle (pedestrian, cyclist or other non-occupant).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS South Carolina Traffic Collision Fact Book, 2024 Edition (Horry County, Part VI pp. 137-138; PDF pp. 145-146); NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) 2020-2024 accident files, STATE 45 / COUNTY 51 (Horry)
verifiedClaims.note: Supported. Optional figure: 'Horry County crashes killed 12 pedestrians in 2024 (SCDPS).' The firm's own Grand Strand Fatal Crash Report states 28.4% vs 20.2% statewide using its own definition; either figure is defensible, keep them consistent if added.

verifiedClaims.claim: The stretch of U.S. 17 through the entertainment districts sees a significant number of DUI-related crashes during late-night hours.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No SCDPS or FARS source reports DUI crashes by road segment or district. County-level: Horry logged 480 non-fatal DUI collisions in 2024 (2,534 in 2020-2024), and SCDPS estimates 25 Horry fatalities in 2024 involved an alcohol-impaired driver (18, 32, 38, 28, 25 in 2020-2024). In 2024, 6 p.m.-midnight carried 21 of the county's 58 fatal collisions.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Fact Book 2024 — Part IV DUI tables (county rows) and Horry County page
verifiedClaims.note: Road-specific claim is unsourced. Suggested: 'Horry County logged 480 DUI-related injury and property-damage crashes in 2024, and an alcohol-impaired driver was involved in an estimated 25 of the county's traffic deaths that year (SCDPS).'

verifiedClaims.claim: Based on crash data from the South Carolina Highway Patrol and local police departments, these intersections consistently produce the highest numbers of collisions in the Grand Strand region.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Horry County Top 5 Intersections by year (SCDPS Fact Books): 2020 — US-501 at S-1224 (Gardner Lacy Rd) 74, SC-9 at S-57 69, US-501 at Carolina Forest Blvd 65, US-17 at SC-544 64, US-501 at S-1315 (Grissom Pkwy) 51; 2021 — US-501 at Carolina Forest Blvd 84, US-501 at SC-544 77, US-501 at S-1224 76, US-17 at SC-544 75, SC-9 at S-57 71; 2022 — SC-9 at S-57 86, US-501 at Carolina Forest Blvd 75, US-501 at SC-544 73, US-17 at SC-544 65, US-501 at Cty-2848 59; 2023 — SC-9 at S-57 91, US-501 at S-1224 71, US-501 at Carolina Forest Blvd 68, US-501 at SC-544 59, US-17 at SC-544 58; 2024 — SC-9 at S-57 116 (0 fatal, 1 serious-injury), US-17 at SC-544 78, US-501 at SC-544 72, US-501 at S-1224 60, US-378 at US-501 59. No fatal collision at any listed intersection in any year. Georgetown County's No. 1 intersection every year 2020-2024 was US-17 at SC-707 (30, 56, 36, 37, 48).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Books, 2020-2024 editions (Horry County Top 5 Roadways/Intersections page in each)
verifiedClaims.note: Only #1 (Carolina Forest Blvd) and #6 (SC 9/Hwy 57) appear in Horry's Top-5 tables, and #7 (US 17 Bypass/SC 707, Murrells Inlet) in Georgetown's. #2, #3, #4 and #5 never appear. Suggested lead: 'South Carolina's annual Traffic Collision Fact Book lists the five highest-crash intersections in each county. These are the Grand Strand intersections that keep appearing on those lists, and others where serious crashes have drawn attention.' Then re-order: SC 9/Hwy 57 first.

verifiedClaims.claim: 1. U.S. 501 and Carolina Forest Boulevard
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Not the region's No. 1 by current data: Horry's top intersection in 2022, 2023 and 2024 was SC 9 at Highway 57 (86, 91, 116 collisions). US-501 at Carolina Forest Blvd ranked 3rd (2020, 65), 1st (2021, 84), 2nd (2022, 75), 3rd (2023, 68) and fell out of the Top 5 in 2024 (fewer than 59).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Books, 2020-2024 editions (Horry County Top 5 Roadways/Intersections page in each)
verifiedClaims.note: Re-number so SC 9 and Highway 57 is #1, or remove the numbers. Note: the Fact Book codes the neighbouring US-501 at S-1224 (Gardner Lacy Rd, 60-76 a year) separately; do not merge them.

verifiedClaims.claim: This intersection has been identified as one of the single most dangerous in the entire Myrtle Beach metropolitan area, producing 65% more car accidents than the second-most hazardous intersection in the region.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No public source for '65% more'. In its best year (2021) it led Horry County by 7 collisions (84 vs 77, about 9%); in 2024 it was not in the Top 5. A Sun News analysis of SCDPS data for 2020-mid-Aug 2024 ranked it tied 9th-10th in Horry County. FARS 2020-2024: no fatal crash coded at US-501/Carolina Forest Blvd.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Books, 2020-2024 editions (Horry County Top 5 Roadways/Intersections page in each); Myrtle Beach Sun News (via Yahoo News), 2024-08-24
verifiedClaims.note: Drop the '65% more' clause (traces only to marketing pages that cite no data). Sun News: https://www.yahoo.com/news/10-most-dangerous-intersections-crashes-100000172.html

verifiedClaims.claim: The explosive residential growth of the Carolina Forest community has pushed commuter traffic volumes at this intersection far beyond its design capacity.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No capacity study for this intersection was found. Horry County's RIDE III list includes U.S. 501 corridor improvements (SC 31 to SC 544) and Carolina Forest Boulevard widening, both aimed at congestion in this area.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: GSATS Policy Committee packet 2025-08-01 (US 501 Corridor Improvements, RIDE III)
verifiedClaims.note: Soften 'far beyond its design capacity' to 'has pushed commuter traffic here to heavy levels, and U.S. 501 through Carolina Forest is slated for widening under the county's RIDE III program.'

verifiedClaims.claim: Rush-hour gridlock, aggressive driving, and red-light running create a near-constant stream of rear-end collisions, T-bone crashes, and sideswipe accidents.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: The Fact Book's intersection table gives counts and severity only (2023: 68 collisions, 1 serious injury, 16 other-injury); no public source gives crash types here.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Books, 2020-2024 editions (Horry County Top 5 Roadways/Intersections page in each)
verifiedClaims.note: 'Near-constant stream' is untraceable. Suggested: 'Congestion and turning conflicts make rear-end and angle crashes common here.'

verifiedClaims.currentValue: Not in any Horry County Top-5 intersection table 2020-2024; FARS 2020-2024 codes no fatal crash at US-501/SC-31. It is a grade-separated interchange. SCDOT 2025 AADT: US 501 SC 31-US 17 Bypass 65,900; SC 31 north of US 501 40,300.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Books, 2020-2024 editions (Horry County Top 5 Roadways/Intersections page in each); NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) 2020-2024 accident files, STATE 45 / COUNTY 51 (Horry); SCDOT AADT 2025

verifiedClaims.claim: The mixing of highway-speed traffic exiting S.C. 31 with congested surface-street traffic on U.S. 501 produces dangerous speed differentials that lead to high numbers of rear-end collisions and angle crashes.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No source gives crash counts or types at this interchange.

verifiedClaims.claim: Known locally as "The Back Gate," this intersection near Market Common has been the site of numerous serious and fatal crashes.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: The Back Gate has been a grade-separated single-point urban interchange since October 2014 ($121.7 million, Riding on a Penny). Not in any Horry Top-5 intersection table 2020-2024. FARS 2020-2024: one fatal crash coded at the interchange frontage (US-17 Bypass at Coventry Blvd, Jan. 2023) and none coded at US-17 Bypass/Farrow Pkwy (a Sept. 2021 'US-17 at Farrow Pkwy' fatal crash is at the Kings Highway end, ~3 km east).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Farrow Parkway (Wikipedia, citing The Sun News); NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) 2020-2024 accident files, STATE 45 / COUNTY 51 (Horry)
verifiedClaims.note: The description is of the pre-2014 at-grade intersection. 'Numerous serious and fatal crashes' is unsupported for 2020-2024. Suggested: 'Known locally as "the Back Gate," the U.S. 17 Bypass junction with Farrow Parkway and S.C. 707 near Market Common was rebuilt as an interchange in 2014 after years of crashes, and it still carries heavy airport, Market Common and bypass traffic.' Or drop the item.

verifiedClaims.claim: The intersection handles heavy traffic from the Market Common mixed-use development, the Myrtle Beach International Airport area, and the Highway 17 Bypass, creating constant conflict between through traffic and vehicles making turning movements.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Since 2014 through traffic on US 17 Bypass passes over the junction on a bridge; turning movements are handled by a single-point interchange and frontage roads (Coventry Blvd).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Farrow Parkway (Wikipedia)
verifiedClaims.note: Delete 'creating constant conflict between through traffic and vehicles making turning movements' (no longer the geometry).

verifiedClaims.claim: Several fatal crashes at this location have drawn community attention and calls for safety improvements.

verifiedClaims.sourceName: Farrow Parkway (Wikipedia); NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) 2020-2024 accident files, STATE 45 / COUNTY 51 (Horry)
verifiedClaims.note: Replace with: 'The 2014 interchange was the county's response to that crash history.' Or delete.

verifiedClaims.claim: The rural feel of this intersection belies its danger — the convergence of two state highways with high speed limits and limited traffic controls produces serious angle collisions.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 2024: 116 collisions, none fatal, 1 serious-injury. FARS 2020-2024 codes no fatal crash here. Highway 57 is secondary route S-57 (SCDOT: 'S- 57 (S HWY 57)'), not an SC primary.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS South Carolina Traffic Collision Fact Book, 2024 Edition (Horry County, Part VI pp. 137-138; PDF pp. 145-146); SCDOT AADT 2025

verifiedClaims.claim: Heavy traffic at this Murrells Inlet intersection leaves motorcycle riders particularly vulnerable.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: US-17 at SC-707 (Murrells Inlet) was GEORGETOWN County's highest-crash intersection every year 2020-2024: 30, 56, 36, 37 and 48 collisions (2024: 0 fatal, 0 serious-injury, 10 other-injury). No intersection-level motorcycle data exists. Horry County 2024: 336 motorcyclists injured or killed, 11 fatally.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: SCDPS Traffic Collision Fact Books, 2020-2024 editions (Horry County Top 5 Roadways/Intersections page in each) (Georgetown County page)
verifiedClaims.note: Keep the item but anchor it in data and the correct county: 'The U.S. 17 Bypass junction with S.C. 707 in Murrells Inlet has been Georgetown County's highest-crash intersection every year since 2020 — 48 collisions in 2024 (SCDPS).' A crash here is filed in Georgetown County, not Horry.

verifiedClaims.claim: U.S. 17 carries more fatal crashes than any other route in Horry County — 39 between 2020 and 2024, against 23 on U.S. 501, according to federal crash records.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: FARS 2020-2024, Horry County, counting every officer-recorded variant of each route (US-17, US-17 Business, US-17 Bypass, Kings Hwy): US 17 — 67 fatal crashes, 71 deaths; US 501 — 36 fatal crashes (37 deaths) as the primary trafficway, 37 including crashes where it is the second road. Next: US 701 and SC 9, 19 each; SC 31, 16. '39' and '23' count only crashes whose road was typed exactly 'US-17' / 'US-501'. SCDPS also ranks US-17 the county's No. 1 roadway every year 2020-2024 (2024: 1,821 collisions, 9 fatal).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS) 2020-2024 accident files, STATE 45 / COUNTY 51 (Horry); SCDPS South Carolina Traffic Collision Fact Book, 2024 Edition (Horry County, Part VI pp. 137-138; PDF pp. 145-146)

verifiedClaims.claim: The highway carries an enormous volume of tourist traffic on weekends and during season transitions, and the long, straight stretches between intersections encourage excessive speed that makes intersection crashes more violent when they occur.
